observation: Two original routes supply 2,836 complete party motion calls: 1,418 active updates and 1,418 inhibited returns. All 729 sweeps, 40 main animation changes, 689 idle shortcuts and 17 sweep rejection stops are computed from entry state. All 5,868 idle predicates agree with source-reviewed compiled m2c output. The four bounded recordings preserve all 119 distinct control artifacts. Twenty-five authored tests pass and 73 corruptions are rejected.
interpretation: The main party movement routine composes original mode selection, prior-motion eligibility, additive velocity, optional pointed bounds, temporary party collision flags, full sweeps, animation changes and signed final motion stores. Only the original 0600 party flag bits are restored after sweeping; stop processing leaves sprite Y motion intact until any later animation change. Later position integration and other actors remain separate.
author: Codex /root, independent original-source Ghidra and execution analysis on 2026-09-08

preconditions: Exact supplied Disc 1/profile, unchanged control/jump and ramp scenarios, original party loader output and separately built uninstrumented controls.
Primary pinned Ghidra 12.1.2 with lab313ru/ghidra_psx_ldr, reviewed partial types and all 507 source-matched selected instructions.

Four source-generated trace specifications remain below callback and payload budgets. Three ramp segments are contiguous windows on one route, not independent scenarios. Original bytes, captured state and decompiler artifacts remain private.
commands: Apply private ReviewActiveMotionTypes.java to the qualified original Ghidra project and export with ExportMainMotionAnalysis.java. Verify the selected source bytes and retain a closed project copy.

Reproduce the retained idle.s/context.c m2c review with --target mipsel-gcc-c --no-cache --stop-on-error. Compile the source-reviewed host body with the two recorded global-input adaptations. No binary match is required or claimed.

Run the corresponding tests/reference-inputs/field23-control-observation.json or field23-ramp-observation.json with tools/reference/scenario.py, the supplied original disc and --trace-instructions <new-private-spec>. The control route also uses its retained original memory sampler. Run each specification in a fresh output directory.
env PYTHONPATH=. python .local/analysis/phase1-active-motion-20260908/negative-active-v2.py (use fresh output versions when repeating)
validation.expected: Exact source, Ghidra, collector/core, entry and return lineage; every selected party effect computed from captured entry inputs and original resource bytes. All controls match; semantic and provenance corruptions are rejected.
validation.actual: All four specifications regenerate exactly and all 36,764 records qualify. Every selected intermediate and return state compares, including complete sprite views, actor bytes, local padding, current-actor global and eight saved registers. All 5,868 compiled C/Python/original predicate results agree. Twenty-five authored tests and 73 fault cases pass; 119 distinct control artifacts are exact.
validation.tolerance: Exact integer, byte, pointer and hash equality over the captured state and documented call relationships. Uncaptured writes, GPU/GTE register state and hardware timing are not claimed.

unobserved_source_branches: Every selected original optional-bounds flag is clear. The enabled pointed quadrilateral, each rejection edge and signed negative-Z packing have authored source-boundary tests only.

Missing-triangle, alternate animation override/inhibition/terrain and selected state boundaries are tested with invented inputs; original execution coverage remains limited to the recorded modes and routes.
NPC or alternate descriptor velocity, resource rebinding/platform/model/frame paths, out-of-range layers and missing party state are explicitly unreconstructed rather than approximated.
limitations: The ramp contains 1,549 excluded complete movement calls for actors 14, 15, 16, 19 and 20. Their idle predicates compare independently; their other movement effects are not claimed.
Fifty-nine external follower animation boundaries are enumerated but not treated as main-motion animation changes in this finding.
Three contiguous ramp observation windows replay the same route; they do not add independent scenario coverage. Two earlier over-budget exploratory recordings are not proof inputs.

A 512-byte sprite capture includes pointed/trailing storage; it is not a complete original structure-size claim. Later position/layer/floor/ceiling/rollback, followers, contact, camera and semantic readiness remain required.
Selective m2c establishes agreement of source-reviewed C, Python and original results. Original compiler identity, binary matching, unobserved runtime branches and hardware timing remain open.
All 15 broad Phase 1 todos and nine slice proof domains remain open. Independent review and native gameplay are not implemented by this finding.
